newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police arrest 26 Kosovo Albanians - agency.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police arrest 26 Kosovo Albanians - agency.

text.p: At least 26 ethnic Albanians were arrested during police raids in Serbia's Kosovo province over the past three days, the Belgrade-based independent news agency Beta reported on Thursday.

The Democratic League of Kosovo, the mainstream party that champions the rights of majority Albanians in the Serbian-ruled region, said 35 people were held in raids on private homes, including members of the local Red Cross.

The League, based in the Kosovo provincial capital Pristina, issued a statement saying large numbers of well-armed police broke furniture and seized personal belongings in daytime and nighttime raids.
Beta said those arrested were mostly political activists and humanitarian workers but gave no further details.
Kosovo has long been regarded by Western political analysts as a potential flashpoint that could undo Balkan peace efforts by the international community.

Informed political sources in Pristina told Reuters this week that moderate Kosovo leaders and the government of Serbia's autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic planned talks to defuse the impasse over the territory's future status.
In 1989 Serbia removed Kosovo's autonomy on the grounds that ethnic Albanians, who outnumber Serbs in the region by nine to one, were preparing to secede.

The independent Belgrade newsletter VIP Report, citing the Democratic League, said the raids were conducted "under the pretext of looking for weapons after several terrorist actions...over the past month.
Serbs and Albanians say 15 Serbs and 14 Albanians were killed in inter-ethnic violence last year alone.
"The Liberation Army of Kosovo has claimed responsibility for the terrorist attacks on ethnic Albanians loyal to the Serbian authorities," the newsletter added.
Little is known of the Liberation Army of Kosovo, and moderate Albanians, including the League, deny all knowledge of it and its members.
